title: Pullback preserves locally finite free internal modules
statement: Let X and Y be schemes, g:Y→X any scheme morphism, and Λ a commutative ring object in condensed abelian groups. An internal module P over condensedRingObj Λ X is locally finite free if a pro-etale scheme cover C of X makes every inverse image of P a finite biproduct of regular modules, allowing varying finite ranks and rank zero. Then the canonical coefficient pullback (CondensedRing.upperStar Λ g).obj P is locally finite free on Y. The coefficient objects and pullbacks are those of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. No etaleness, noetherianity, nonemptiness or finite-dimensional field hypothesis is required. The accompanying reusable API also transports the same scheme-cover predicate along module isomorphisms and invertible coefficient maps.

source.place: Section 6.8, local finite freeness under inverse image; Stacks Project, Modules on Sites, Tag 03DO

proof.text: Reuse free_comap, free_of_iso, free_of_comap and free_pullback_comp_iff from CondensedFieldLfpLocalTriviality through import all. For coefficient restriction, keep the original cover and apply the free_comap theorem and the mapModComapIso comparison on each member. Module isomorphisms transport the same finite free presentations. These are the existing proved helpers, not additional lattice existence assumptions.

Map the finite biproduct presentation of a free module through the additive strong monoidal inverse-image functor. Its mapBiproduct comparison and the regular-module comparison give a free presentation on Y. Base change the trivializing scheme cover C. The pullback-square equality, together with free_pullback_comp_iff, identifies each pulled-back trivialization with the restriction of the pulled-back module.

The canonical condensed coefficient pullback is extension of scalars along condensedPullbackHom after ordinary inverse image. That coefficient morphism is invertible. Apply locallyFree_comap to its inverse and then the extendScalarsIsoComapInv isomorphism, using locallyFree_of_iso. This proves the exact raw scheme-cover predicate, including empty schemes and rank zero.
